approach: A moderator slows down the fast neutrons released in fission so that they are more likely to cause further fission in uranium-235, sustaining the chain reaction.

steps.text: Recall that fission releases fast neutrons, but slow (thermal) neutrons are far more effective at causing further fission in uranium-235.
steps.equation: fast neutrons must be slowed to sustain the chain reaction

steps.text: The moderator, such as heavy water or graphite, slows down these fast neutrons through repeated collisions, without absorbing them.
steps.equation: moderator: slows fast neutrons to thermal energies

common_mistakes.text: Confusing the role of the moderator with the role of control rods, which absorb excess neutrons to control the reaction rate.
Confusing the moderator with the coolant, which removes the heat generated in the reactor.
